note.explanation: Energy sources can be compared by whether they can be replaced, their cost, and the pollution or other problems they cause.
examples: Hydroelectric power is economical and pollution free.
Burning fossil fuels releases smoke, carbon dioxide and heat.
note.checkAnswer: Fossil fuels are non-renewable and burning them causes pollution.
note.simple: Some energy sources can be replaced and cause little pollution. Others run out or create pollution and other risks.
note.checkQuestion: Name one problem caused by burning fossil fuels.
note.title: Comparing methods of energy production
steps: Check whether it is renewable or non-renewable.
Compare its cost and pollution or other disadvantages.
note.answer: Hydroelectric power is economical and pollution free, while burning fossil fuels pollutes the environment.

options: It is economical and pollution free.

This is incorrect because radioactive waste is discussed as a problem of nuclear power.

This is incorrect because the section does not say hydroelectric power needs fossil fuels.

rationales: This is incorrect because the section says these methods need more initial cost.

written.text: Differentiate between renewable and non-renewable energy sources.
written.finalAnswer: Renewable sources can be replenished; non-renewable sources are limited and cannot be replaced quickly.

examTips: This topic is likely to appear as a short-answer comparison of renewable and non-renewable sources or as a question about advantages and disadvantages.
For a comparison question, state a clear difference and give suitable examples if asked.
For an advantages-and-disadvantages answer, name the energy method and connect each point to it, such as smoke and carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels.
For nuclear power, include both radioactive leakage risk and the problem of disposing of nuclear waste when relevant.

example.question: How does your textbook compare hydroelectric power with power generated by fossil fuels and nuclear fuel?
example.answer: Hydroelectric power is economical and pollution free; fossil fuels pollute the atmosphere, while nuclear power has radioactive leakage and waste-disposal risks. This section does not provide a numbered worked example, so this comparison models an answer using its text.

explain.title: Hydroelectric power
explain.body: The production of hydroelectric power is more economical and pollution free.

explain.title: Solar, wind, tidal and wave power
explain.body: These methods need more initial cost, but they do not produce pollution and are economical as well. Windmills can be very noisy, and some people think wind turbines spoil the beauty of the landscape.

explain.title: Fossil fuels
explain.body: Power generation by fossil fuels adds to environmental pollution. Burning fossil fuels produces smoke, carbon dioxide gas and heat, which directly pollute the atmosphere.

explain.title: Nuclear power and thermal pollution
explain.body: Nuclear generators use steam produced by nuclear heat energy. Heat itself is a form of pollution, and radioactive leakage can harm living bodies. Disposal of nuclear waste is another problem. Waste energy eventually becomes thermal energy in the environment, contributing to thermal pollution and global warming.

mistakes: Do not say that renewable sources always have no disadvantages; the section mentions the initial cost of solar, wind, tidal and wave power and the noise of windmills.
Do not confuse radioactive leakage, which is a nuclear power risk, with smoke and carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels.
Do not state that all energy sources have the same cost or pollution effects.
When discussing wood as renewable, mention that trees must be replanted or allowed to grow again.
